statements.__comment__: DEPRECATED: temporary backward-compatibility migration; remove in v1.0.0. CVEMetadata enriched every :CVE S1AppFinding. The next statement removes that label, after which CVEMetadata cleanup, which matches :CVE targets, can no longer reach these edges, so delete them first. Scoped to the findings of the account that just synced, and only to findings that already link to their S1Vulnerability, so a site-scoped sync that skips cleanup leaves findings it did not read untouched. Idempotent: findings no longer get ENRICHES edges. Each run deletes up to $SCAN_LIMIT_SIZE edges from one scan of the account, committing every $LIMIT_SIZE, so a large account is not rescanned once per batch.
statements.query: MATCH (:S1Account {id: $S1_ACCOUNT_ID})-[:RESOURCE]->(f:S1AppFinding:CVE)-[:HAS_VULNERABILITY]->(:S1Vulnerability) MATCH (f)<-[r:ENRICHES]-(:CVEMetadata) WITH r LIMIT $SCAN_LIMIT_SIZE CALL (r) { DELETE r } IN TRANSACTIONS OF $LIMIT_SIZE ROWS

statements.__comment__: DEPRECATED: temporary backward-compatibility migration; remove in v1.0.0. Earlier releases put the :CVE ontology label, with its _ont_* fields, on every S1AppFinding. The CVE is now the S1Vulnerability the finding links to, and nothing updates these any more, so strip them: left stale, :CVE queries count each SentinelOne CVE once per affected endpoint. Scoped like the statement above. Idempotent: once stripped, no S1AppFinding carries :CVE. Batched like the statement above, for the same reason.
statements.query: MATCH (:S1Account {id: $S1_ACCOUNT_ID})-[:RESOURCE]->(f:S1AppFinding:CVE)-[:HAS_VULNERABILITY]->(:S1Vulnerability) WITH f LIMIT $SCAN_LIMIT_SIZE CALL (f) { REMOVE f:CVE, f._ont_source, f._ont_cve_id, f._ont_base_severity } IN TRANSACTIONS OF $LIMIT_SIZE ROWS

name: SentinelOne - migrate CVE labels written by earlier versions
